questions.question: What is the cause of the apparent elevation of a star's position when viewed near the horizon?

options.text: The gravitational force of Earth on starlight
Reflection of starlight away from the normal
Atmospheric refraction of starlight towards the normal

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atmospheric refraction of starlight towards the normal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Atmospheric refraction is the bending of light as it passes through Earth's atmosphere, causing the apparent position of the star to change.
 
• This refraction occurs because the atmosphere's density varies with altitude, causing a change in the speed of light.
 
• When starlight enters the Earth's atmosphere at a shallow angle near the horizon, it bends more significantly towards the normal (the perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence).
 
• This bending makes the star appear higher in the sky than its true geometric position.
 
• Atmospheric refraction is more pronounced near the horizon compared to when a star is overhead due to the increased thickness of the atmosphere the light passes through.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Refraction:**

 
 
• Refraction is the change in direction of a wave passing from one medium to another caused by its change in speed.
 
• In the context of atmospheric refraction, the medium changes from the vacuum of space to the Earth's atmosphere.
 
 
 
• **Snell's Law:**
 
 
• Snell's Law describes how the angle of incidence and the angle of refraction are related for a wave crossing the interface between two media with different refractive indices.
 
• It is given by the formula: n1 * sin(θ1) = n2 * sin(θ2), where n1 and n2 are the refractive indices of the two media, and θ1 and θ2 are the angles of incidence and refraction, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Apparent Position:**
 
 
• The apparent position of an object is where it appears to be located, which can differ from its true position due to effects such as refraction.
 
• For stars near the horizon, their apparent position is higher than their true position due to atmospheric refraction.
 
 
 
• **Atmospheric Layers:**
 
 
• The Earth's atmosphere is composed of several layers, each with different densities and temperatures, affecting the refraction of light.
 
• The main layers include the troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, and thermosphere, with the majority of atmospheric refraction occurring in the troposphere.
 
 
 
• **Mirage:**
 
 
• A mirage is another optical phenomenon caused by the refraction of light through layers of air at different temperatures.
 
• It often occurs in deserts or on hot roads, where light bends to create the illusion of water or other images.

questions.question: An object is placed at a distance of 10 cm in front of a double convex lens made of glass of refractive index 1.5. Both the radii of curvature of the lens are 20 cm in magnitude. What is the position of the image formed?
questions.solution:
__**Calculations**__:

Given,

Distance of the object from the lens = u = -10 cm

Refractive index of the lens = µ = 1.5

The Radii of curvature of the lens are 20 cm in magnitude

R₁ = 20 cm and R₂ = -20 cm (As per sign convention)

According to Len's Maker's formula

(1)/(f)=(mu - 1)((1)/(R₁)-(1)/(R₂))=(1.5-1)((1)/(20)-(1)/(-20))\ =0.5 times (2)/(20)=(1)/(20)\ or, f=20 cm 

From the Lens equation,

(1)/(v)-(1)/(u)=(1)/(f)\ (1)/(v)=(1)/(f)+(1)/(u)\ or, v=(fu)/(u+f)=(20 times (-10))/(-10+20)=(-200)/(10)=-20 cm

__**The image is formed 20 cm on the same side as the object.**__

 **Examples of Total Internal Reflection **

 
 
• 
 Sparkling of Diamond

 Formation of Mirage
 
 
 
 
• When white light is passed through a glass prism it splits into its spectrum of colors (in order violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange, and red) and this process of white light splitting into its constituent colors is termed as **dispersion**.

• **Total internal reflection (TIR):**

 
 
• When a wave travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium,** it bends away from the normal and as the angle of incidence increases in the denser medium**, the angle of refraction in the rarer medium also increases and at a certain angle the angle of refraction becomes 90°. The angle of incidence is called the **critical angle (C)**.
 
• When the angle of incidence becomes greater than the critical angle, the light ray returns to the same medium after reflection from the interface. This phenomenon is called** total internal reflection (TIR)**.

questions.question: Which type of mirror is used as reflectors in torches, vehicle headlights to get the powerful beams of light?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Concave mirror**__.

__
 
• A **concave mirror or converging mirror** is a spherical mirror, which has a reflecting surface which bends inwards. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

• A concave mirror is used as a reflector in torches, searchlights, headlights of motor vehicles, etc. to get a powerful parallel beam of light. 
 
• This helps us to see things up to a considerable distance in the darkness of night.
 
• Some dental mirrors also use a concave surface to provide a magnified image.

questions.question: A concave lens has a focal length 15 cm. If the object is placed at 30 cm from the lens, what is the image distance?
questions.solution:
Option **2** is the correct answer: 

__CONCEPT__:

__
 
• **Lens**: The transparent curved surface which is used to refract the light and make an image of any object placed in front of it is called a lens.
 
• Concave lens: It is a diverging lens that diverges the parallel beam of light.
 
 
• It can also gather light from all directions and project it as a parallel beam.
 
• It has a virtual focus from the diverging rays of light that seem to converge.
 
• The image formed by a concave lens is virtual, erect, and diminished.
 
 

The **lens equation** which gives the relation between focal length, the distance of image and object from the lens is

{1 over f} = {{1 over v }-{1 over u}}

where f is the focal length, u is the distance of the object from the lens and v is that of the image from the lens.

**CALCULATION**__:

__
 
• The **focal length of a concave lens is taken negative** (is measured opposite to the incident rays).

Given that:

focal length f = -15 cm

Distance of object u = - 30 cm

{1 over v} = {{1 over f }+{1 over u}}

substituting these values in the lens equation we get,

{1 over v} = {-{1 over 15}-{1 over 30}}

{1 over v}={-2-1 over 30}

{1 over v}={-3 over 30}

v=-10cm

Hence **distance of the object from the lens is 10 cm and the negative sign signifies a virtual image**. So option 2 is correct.

**EXTRA POINTS**__:

Positions of the object and image for the concave lens:

 
 

 Position of the object
 Position of the image
 The relative size of the image
 Nature of the image
 
 

 1. At infinity
 At focus F1
 Highly diminished, point-sized
 Virtual and erect
 
 

 2. Between infinity and optical centre O of the lens
 Between focus F1 and optical centre O
 Diminished
 Virtual and erect

questions.question: Which colour of light from VIBGYOR has minimum energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Red.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The energy of light is** inversely proportional** to its wavelength.
 
• Therefore, the light with the **longest wavelength,** i.e. **red**, has the **least energy.**
 
• The colours of VIBGYOR are arranged in **increasing order** of their** wavelengths.**
 
• Hence, **violet** has the** highest energy **and red has the least.
 
• **Green** is the colour of light with a wavelength between yellow and blue.
 
• It has **more energy** than yellow but less than blue.
 
• **Yellow** is the colour of light with a wavelength between green and orange.
 
• It has** less energy** than green but more than orange.

• **VIBGYOR** stands for** Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, and Red.**

 
 
• These are the** seven colours **of the visible spectrum of light.
 
 
 
• Violet has the **shortest wavelength** and the highest energy among the colours of VIBGYOR.
 
• **Indigo** is a colour that lies between **blue and violet **in the spectrum.
 
 
• It is not always distinguishable from blue and is **not** considered a separate colour by some people.
 
 
 
• **Orange** is a colour that lies between **yellow and red** in the spectrum.
 
 
• It has **more energy** than red but less than yellow.

questions.question: A-ray of light travelling from a denser medium to a rarer medium

options.text: slows down and bends away from the normal,
slows down and bends towards the normal.
speeds up and bends away from the normal.
speeds up and bends towards the normal.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**speeds up and bends away from the normal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Refraction

 
• It is the bending of light rays after entering a medium where its speed is different.
 
• Due to the refraction of light, when a ray of light passes from a rarer medium to a denser medium, bends towards the normal boundary between the two media. The amount of bending depends on the indices of refraction of the two media. 
 
• A ray of light traveling from a rarer medium to a denser medium slows down and bends towards the normal. 
 
• When it travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium, it speeds up and bends away from the normal. Hence, Option 3 is correct.
 
• The angle of refraction or the amount of bending of light depends on the refractive index (μ) of the two media.
 
• When light passes through a low refractive index, like air (faster medium or optically rarer medium) to a high refractive index, like glass(slower medium or optically denser medium), its speed decreases and bends towards the normal. 
 
• When light passes through a high refractive index, like glass (slower medium or optically denser medium) to a low refractive index, like air (faster medium or optically rarer medium) its speed increases and bends away from the normal. 
 
•

questions.question: An incident ray strikes a plane mirror at an angle of 20° with the mirror. The angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray is ________.
questions.solution:
**__Laws of reflection:__**

1. The angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.

2. The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal lie in the same plane.

3. The reflected ray and the incident ray are on opposite sides of the normal.

__
 
• Angle of reflection = ∠r
 
• Angle of incidence = ∠i
 
• The angle between the plane mirror and incident ray = 20°

According Law of reflection:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ba310ec8a33b6876833335a27b7097d2a4c6dd55c6f634934519a02c7c8ffb23.png] 

 
• 20° + ∠r + ∠i + 20° = 180°
 
• ∠r + ∠i = 140°
 
• The angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray is **140°.__**

questions.question: What is the refractive index of air?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1.0003**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The refractive index of air is approximately **1.0003**.
 
• The refractive index is a measure of how much the speed of light is reduced inside a medium.
 
• Air, being a very low-density medium compared to other substances like water or glass, has a refractive index very close to 1.
 
• This value implies that light travels almost as fast in air as it does in a vacuum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The refractive index of a medium is calculated using the formula **n = c / v**, where **c** is the speed of light in a vacuum and **v** is the speed of light in the medium.
 
• In most practical scenarios, the refractive index of air is taken as 1 for simplicity, but the precise value is **1.0003**.
 
• Other common refractive indices include water with a value of approximately 1.33 and glass with values ranging from 1.5 to 1.9 depending on the type.
 
• The small deviation from 1 for air is due to its density and the slight delay it causes in the propagation of light.

questions.question: Rainbow is a natural phenomenon which shows:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**dispersion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A rainbow is formed due to the **dispersion of light** when it passes through water droplets in the atmosphere.
 
• Dispersion causes the white sunlight to split into its constituent colors (VIBGYOR - Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, and Red).
 
• The process of dispersion involves the **bending of light** rays at different angles when they enter and exit the water droplets, resulting in a spectrum of colors.
 
• The phenomenon of a rainbow can be observed when the sun is low in the sky and behind the observer, and rain is falling in front of them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diffraction**

 
 
• Diffraction is the bending of light waves around the edges of an obstacle or aperture.
 
• This phenomenon occurs with all types of waves, including light, sound, and water waves.
 
• An example of diffraction is the spreading of light when it passes through a small slit.
 
 
 
• **Refraction**
 
 
• Refraction is the change in direction of light when it passes from one medium to another of different density.
 
• This bending of light is due to the change in speed of light in different mediums.
 
• An example of refraction is the bending of light when it passes from air into water, making objects appear bent or distorted.
 
 
 
• **Reflection**
 
 
• Reflection is the bouncing back of light rays when they hit a surface.
 
• The angle of incidence (incoming angle) is equal to the angle of reflection (outgoing angle).
 
• An example of reflection is the image seen in a mirror.

questions.question: When a ray of light travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium, it bends ________.

options.text: Towards the normal and slows down
Away from the normal and slow down
Towards the normal and speeds up
Away from the normal and speeds up

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option **4.**

__
 
• When a ray of light travels from a **denser medium to a rarer medium**, it bends **away from the normal and speeds up__.**
 
• When a ray of light passes from a denser to a rarer medium, the angle of refraction would be greater than the angle of incidence as the light ray bends away from the normal.
 
• The amount of bending depends on the indices of refraction of the two media.
 
• **Snell's law** is a formula used to describe the relationship between the angles of incidence and refraction when referring to light or other waves passing through a boundary between two different isotropic media.

questions.question: Ramu has been given a tub of water with a refractive index of 1.33, a mug of oil with a refractive index of 1.46, a bottle of glycerine with a refractive index of 1.5 and a glass-slab with a refractive index of 1.65. Light will travel fastest in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Light travels fastest in a medium with the lowest refractive index.
 
• Water has the lowest refractive index (1.33) among the given options.
 
• A lower refractive index indicates that the medium is less optically dense, allowing light to travel through it more quickly.
 
• Compared to oil (1.46), glycerine (1.5), and glass-slab (1.65), water provides the least resistance to the propagation of light.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Refractive Index**

 
 
• The refractive index of a material is a measure of how much the speed of light is reduced inside the medium compared to the speed of light in a vacuum.
 
• The formula for refractive index (n) is n = c/v, where c is the speed of light in a vacuum and v is the speed of light in the medium.
 
 
 
• **Speed of Light in Different Media**
 
 
• The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately 299,792 km/s.
 
• In materials with higher refractive indices, the speed of light is slower.
 
 
 
• **Optical Density**
 
 
• Optical density refers to how much a material can slow down light. Materials with higher refractive indices are optically denser.
 
• Water, being less optically dense compared to oil, glycerine, and glass, allows light to travel faster through it.
 
 
 
• **Applications**
 
 
• Understanding the refractive index is crucial in designing lenses, optical instruments, and various scientific applications.
 
• It helps in determining how light will behave when transitioning between different media.

questions.question: When a ray of light is incident on a reflecting surface and if the reflected ray is at an angle of 90° to the incident ray, the angle of incidence of the ray is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**45​°**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Law of reflection:** The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of refraction.​
 
• Let us suppose-
 
 
• ∠i = angle of incidence
 
• ∠r = angle of reflection
 
 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cb705b2ac8e34be87b858ed04cdd6cd94e688eda7c2558bcac1fa4d807d9ce25.png] 

 
• According to the law of reflection, the angle of incidence is equal to the angle of refraction.
 
 
• That is, ∠i=∠r. (Let it be x).
 
 
 
• **In this case, the difference between the angle of incidence and angle of reflection is 90 degrees**.
 
 
• Given, ∠i+∠r = 90°
 
• or, x+x=90°
 
• or, x=45°
 
 
 
• **Hence, the angle of incidence is 45°**.

questions.question: The band of the color component of light beam is called its ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Spectrum**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The band of the color component of a light beam is referred to as its **spectrum**.
 
• A spectrum is a range of colors produced when light is dispersed by a prism or diffraction grating, showing the constituent wavelengths of the light source.
 
• It is a fundamental concept in the study of light and optics, helping to understand the composition and properties of light.
 
• Spectrums can be observed in various phenomena such as rainbows, where light is dispersed by water droplets.
 
• Different types of spectra include continuous spectrum, emission spectrum, and absorption spectrum, each providing different information about the light source.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frequency** refers to the number of oscillations or cycles per second of a wave, measured in Hertz (Hz).
 
• **Bandwidth** is the range of frequencies within a given band, particularly that used for transmitting a signal.
 
• **Wavelength** is the distance between successive crests of a wave, typically measured in meters.
 
• The term **spectrum** is also used in other contexts, such as the electromagnetic spectrum, which includes a range of all types of electromagnetic radiation.
 
• Understanding the spectrum of light is crucial in fields like astronomy, chemistry, and physics, where it helps in identifying the composition of distant stars, chemical substances, and more.
